newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - May 30.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- STORM OVER THE LENGTH OF A TRAIN

A dispute about how long it takes drivers to walk the length of a train today threatened to cause disruption to hundreds of commuter services in and out of London. The result of a ballot of London train drivers on whether to take industrial action will be announced next Thursday.

-- CITY SPLIT ON CHANCE OF RISE IN BASE RATE The City is divided on the question of whether the Bank of England's new monetary committee will decide on an immediate rise in base rates at its first meeting next week. The Bank's inflation report said that a further rise in rates was required, but the committee might want to delay such a move until after the contents of Chancellor Gordon Brown's Budget are known and the other four members of the committee are appointed.
-- GALLAHER SET FOR LONDON MARKET DEBUT

Gallaher, the cigarettes group which owns Benson & Hedges, is due to start trading on the London Stock Exchange this week, with industry analysts predicting its market value will propel it straight into the top 100 British companies. The company is also due to appear in the High Court, in a case brought by litigating British smokers which could result in both Gallaher and Imperial Tobacco being dragged through the courts.

Whitbread today signed a deal with Young & Co whereby Young's 170 tied pubs will sell draught Stella Artois, Whitbread's premium lager, in addition to the bottled product that the chain already sells.

Hideo Sakamaki, the former president of Japan's Nomura Securities, was arrested today over payments to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer. The arrest impacted the Tokyo share market, which fell flat after a small early-morning rally. The Nikkei 225 index was 57 points down at 20,255, with an hour's trading left.
